candidate.answerReason: An upward-opening parabola lies strictly above the x-axis exactly when it has no real zeros, which requires \(\Delta<0\). Thus the answer is B; \(\Delta=0\) would permit contact with the axis.

methods.label: Relate axis intersections to the discriminant
methods.explanation: The entire graph lies above the axis only when there are no intersection points, so the discriminant is less than 0. When it equals 0, the graph touches the \(x\)-axis.
methods.levelReason: Uses familiar quadratic graph and discriminant properties from grade 9, within the stated scope.
